name: qjs_class_ids
prototype: struct { unsigned class_id; const char *name; } qjs_class_ids[]

ownership.argument: Class ids measured on a live p67 runtime by allocating a marked object of each kind and reading the class_id word at object+6, the same field qjs_is_function 0xC27DA88 dispatches on: ArrayBuffer = 19, Uint8Array = 23, Uint16Array = 25. They are consecutive in the QuickJS class order, which is the sanity check that the field is really the class id and not an incidental small integer.

provenance.source: Mirage probe-p67, firmware 3.101.043. A staged script allocated ArrayBuffer(512) filled 0xA7, ArrayBuffer(8) filled 0x5C and Uint16Array(16) filled 0x5C5C; one PSRAM snapshot at 0x3C000000 was searched for the payloads and for records whose refcount is small, whose +6 word is a plausible class id and which contain the payload pointer plus its length. ArrayBuffer resolved to a record with class 19 (data at +0x54, byte length at +0x58), Uint8Array to 23 and Uint16Array to 25, both typed arrays with the payload at +0x24 and the element count at +0x28. The static side shows 19 as the creation immediate in js_new_array_buffer 0xC2D34C8 and 152 = 19*8 as the prototype-table offset.

notes: Only the ids are claimed here; the three wrapper addresses they unlock are still open, because the wrappers have to be picked by their own shape.
